title: Mahatma Gandhi and Madan Mohan Malaviya: The Banaras Hindu University Endowment Drive
summary: During the historic fundraising drive for Banaras Hindu University, Mahatma Gandhi and Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya exchanged brilliant banter on public accountability and educational service.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 140: காந்தியும் மதன் மோகன் மாளவியாவும்: “25 ஆண்டுகளை உங்கள் கணக்கில் சேருங்கள்!”
full_text:
In 1916, following the grand inauguration of Banaras Hindu University, Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya—fondly venerated as 'Mahamana'—was exhausted after years of relentless nationwide travel to secure endowments from princes and commoners alike.

Meeting Mahatma Gandhi, Malaviya sighed with a mixture of satisfaction and weariness:
"Gandhiji, I have poured every ounce of my energy into collecting funds for this university so our youth may access science and culture. Once the remaining debts are cleared and the endowment is secure, my life’s work will be finished. I shall gladly welcome retirement, or even death!"

Gandhi smiled warmly and placed a hand on Malaviya’s shoulder:
"Mahamana, do not contemplate retirement so easily! Building the university was only the foundation. But who will build the free India in which these educated youth must live? You must add at least twenty-five more active years to your life’s ledger! Do not deduct them for rest; credit them to the account of Swaraj. Brick and mortar do not make a nation—courageous, free citizens do!"

Malaviya laughed heartily at Gandhi’s spirited rejoinder. Both statesmen recognized that education without civic freedom is incomplete, and freedom without education is unsustainable.
